clue.text: Shiraz nearly swamping Iran's capital and land to the west

indicators.note: swamping means the shortened wine surrounds the next piece
nearly says the wine's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Shiraz is the grape also known as Syrah

indicators.note: a capital is the head or first letter of the word Iran's

explanation.surface: A glass of Persian red seems to engulf Iran's capital city and lands further west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims SYRAH to SYRA, and 'swamping' puts the I from 'Iran's capital' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The country lies to the west of Iran, across Iraq, so it is a land to the west.

clue.text: What can make neat lines sit incongruously with the ragged

indicators.note: incongruously says the letters of sit and the ragged are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tidy person sits awkwardly among scruffy people.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler used for drawing straight lines makes them neat.

clue.text: Char lady

definitions.meaning: char is slang for tea, and ... Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Char lady' suggests a cleaning woman, but each word is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name that also, via rhyming slang Rosie Lee, means a cup of tea.

clue.text: Before second son, take liberty with eternal vigilance

indicators.note: before says the rearranged piece comes ahead of the next two letters
taking liberties with the word eternal means rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Before a second son, someone takes liberties with constant watchfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take liberty with' turns ETERNAL into ALERTNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigilance means watchful attention, a near synonym of being alert.

clue.text: Crepe twisted around because of necessity

indicators.note: around says the rearranged crepe goes round the next piece
twisted says the letters of crepe are rearranged

parts.note: for can mean because, as in 'for he was tired'

explanation.surface: A piece of crumpled crepe fabric gets wrapped around something out of need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges the fabric's letters as PERCE, and 'around' wraps them round the short word; the definition is 'of necessity', borrowing 'of' from the surface's 'because of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce is a literary adverb meaning by necessity or unavoidably.

clue.text: State school's change of administration

parts.note: to put something is to state it, as in 'put it plainly'
SCH is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A state school's board is overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State school' reads as a publicly funded school; 'State' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden coup, a violent change of government.

clue.text: Racy writer reduced advance to cover Third Man

indicators.note: to cover says the shortened word goes round the next piece
reduced says the word for advance loses its last letter

parts.note: to raise can mean to advance or put forward
Abel, son of Adam and Eve, was the third man in Genesis

explanation.surface: A risque author is paid a smaller advance to write about the film The Third Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the last letter of the verb, and 'to cover' wraps the rest round Genesis's third man; The Third Man is also a famous film, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Renaissance author of Gargantua is known for bawdy comic writing.

clue.text: Dirty but cleared of sulphur and protected from rust?

indicators.note: cleared of says the sulphur letter is removed

parts.note: soiled means dirty
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Something dirty but cleaned of sulphur is also protected against corrosion.
explanation.definitionFit: Coating metal with lubricant prevents rust; the question mark marks this as one example.

clue.text: In a stupor, chap needs an invigorating medicine

parts.note: cat is old slang for a man or chap
an is the indefinite article, giving A
a tonic is an invigorating medicine

explanation.surface: A man in a daze needs a pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonic describes being in an immobile, unresponsive state like a stupor.

clue.text: Decent state seeing cities be partly rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters of these words are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Respectability is achieved as cities are partly reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being decent and respected is the condition named by this abstract noun.

clue.text: Not being nice, when three numbers are entered for one, one flipped

indicators.note: entered for says the numbers take the place of the numeral in nice

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
the first of the three numbers is one

indicators.note: one flipped says one of the numbers is written backwards

parts.note: the second of the three numbers is six
the third of the three numbers is ten

explanation.surface: Being unpleasant, someone puts three numbers in for one and flips one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered for' swaps the numeral in nice for three spelt-out numbers; 'one flipped' turns the middle one round to XIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonexistence is the state of not being at all.

clue.text: Same chip oddly back in one of teeth …

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in puts the reversed letters inside the adjective for teeth

parts.note: dental means relating to teeth

indicators.note: back says those picked letters are read in reverse
oddly picks the first and third letters of chip

explanation.surface: A dentist finds the same chip in one tooth again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first and third letters of chip, 'back' turns them round, and 'in' sets them inside the teeth adjective; the ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical things are exactly the same as each other, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: … and here you've partly chipped it too

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Continuing the dental story, the same tooth has been damaged a little here as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the previous clue, whose answer means 'same'; this clue says the same again.
explanation.definitionFit: Said to mean the same thing again, the word repeats what came before, as here you've had it twice.

clue.text: Go on parking in hospital area enclosure

indicators.note: in says the parking letter goes inside the hospital, area and enclosure letters

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Drivers are told to continue to the parking spot within the hospital's fenced-off area.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on is to take place or occur, the same as this verb.

clue.text: Press on, essentially, always getting involved

parts.note: per se means in itself or essentially

indicators.note: getting involved says the letters of the word for always are tangled

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: Essentially, one should always keep going when getting involved.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty, to press on.

clue.text: Trading floor beat church's meagre pay

parts.note: the pit is the trading floor of a stock or commodity exchange
to tan someone's hide is to beat them
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A trader on the floor beats the church's poor wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a very small or inadequate sum of money paid.

clue.text: Time with glimmering?

parts.note: a glimmering is a faint inkling or hint

explanation.surface: A moment marked by a faint glimmer of light.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a twinkling is a brief time, and also a glimmering light.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinkling is an instant, and twinkling light glimmers, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Band's improvisation conveyed energy for boisterous party

parts.note: a jam is an improvised session by a band
bore is the past tense of bear, to carry or convey

explanation.surface: A band's improvised session brought energy to a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large, lively celebration or gathering.

clue.text: Train laboratory animal and then regret looking back

indicators.note: looking back says the whole run of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: the rat is the classic animal used in laboratories
so can mean and then, as in 'so we went home'
to rue something is to regret it

explanation.surface: Someone trains a lab animal and then later regrets it, looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' turns RATSORUE into the answer; 'Train' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the high-speed passenger train running through the Channel Tunnel.

clue.text: Head off sudden irregularity with island's exotic fruit

indicators.note: head off says the first letter of the word for a sudden irregularity is removed

parts.note: a glitch is a sudden malfunction or irregularity

explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like 'prevent' but means drop the first letter, G.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variant spelling of lychee, a sweet fruit from China.

clue.text: Perhaps a Danish aide's shot

a shot is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: Perhaps a Danish citizen's assistant took a shot.

explanation.definitionFit: A Danish is a sweet baked item, one example of this baked dough.

clue.text: Visitors taking time out to speculate

parts.note: guests are visitors

clue.text: Stalk that provides support

a structural bar bracing a framework

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalk' tempts as a plant stem, but it is the swaggering walk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a swaggering walk and a supporting brace in a structure.

clue.text: Bishop has no great stomach for accident site

a pot is a large belly, as in pot-belly

explanation.surface: A slim bishop has no paunch for the place where crashes happen.

clue.text: One of many irons in the fire for stud, say?

definitions.text: One of many irons in the fire
definitions.meaning: a metal rod for stirring a fire, one of the fireside irons
stud is a variety of a card game played for money

clue.text: Mistakes are deceiving among a number gripped by fear

clue.text: "Light" and "hefty" are different

clue.text: Overindulge, knocking back Ecstasy and booze

parts.note: E is slang for the drug Ecstasy
grog is slang for alcoholic drink
